newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus parliament approves Ling as prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Belarus parliament approves Ling as prime minister.

text.p: Belarus deputies approved Sergei Ling, acting head of government since November, to the full post of prime minister on Wednesday.
Deputies in parliament, following a request from President Alexander Lukashenko, voted 97 to eight to approve Ling's candidacy.
Lukashenko praised Ling as he proposed him to the chamber, referring to his "honesty and decency" and long years occupying top economic posts in the former Soviet republic of 10 million.
Ling, 59, was appointed acting prime minister on November 18 after his predecessor Mikhail Chigir resigned over his opposition to a controversial referendum, which boosted Lukashenko's powers.

A former head of the state prices committee and deputy head of Gosplan which controlled the Soviet-era economy, Ling became deputy prime minister in charge of the economy when the Soviet Union collapsed. In 1994 he was named economy minister.
